evidence.title: RECIPE CARD - AF-12 anti-rust alkyd enamel
evidence.claim: Step is in the current recipe (RECIPE CARD - AF-12 anti-rust alkyd enamel).
evidence.quote: 4. Add 1.6 kg ammonium chloride (RM-118) pre-dissolved in 4 L water; stir 10 min.

evidence.title: RECIPE CARD - AF-12 anti-rust alkyd enamel
evidence.claim: Earliest archived recipe revision containing the step is dated 1996-01-22.
evidence.quote: 4. Add 0.8 kg ammonium chloride per 1000 kg batch, dissolved in 2 L water; stir 10 min.

evidence.title: CHANGE REQUEST CR-1995-009
evidence.claim: In 1995, ammonium chloride was added to AF-12 to prevent livering caused by high alkalinity in Cromopigmenti Lazzeretti's CL-77 pigment.
evidence.quote: livering of AF-12 caused by the high free alkalinity of chromate pigment CL-77 supplied by Cromopigmenti Lazzeretti

evidence.title: CHANGE REQUEST CR-1995-009
evidence.claim: The 1995 addition of ammonium chloride was intended as a temporary measure until the supplier met the 0.30% alkalinity specification.
evidence.quote: temporary - to be reviewed when the supplier delivers pigment within the 0.30 % alkalinity specification

evidence.title: CHANGE REQUEST CR-1996-003
evidence.claim: In 1996, livering caused by alkaline chromate pigment remained a risk, requiring a 12-hour rest period to detect it.
evidence.quote: detect livering caused by alkaline chromate pigment before the batch is filled

evidence.title: DEVIATION REPORT DR-1995-031
evidence.claim: In 1995, AF-12 batches suffered from livering (rubbery gel formation) after 4-6 weeks of storage, leading to customer returns.
evidence.quote: tins opened after 4 to 6 weeks of storage show the enamel thickened into a rubbery gel ("livering")

evidence.title: DEVIATION REPORT DR-1995-031
evidence.claim: In 1995, livering was suspected to be caused by basic lead chromate pigment lots CL-77/95-09 and CL-77/95-10 from Cromopigmenti Lazzeretti.
evidence.quote: Suspected cause: reaction between the acid groups of the alkyd and the basic lead chromate pigment

evidence.title: LABORATORY TEST REPORT LT-1995-118
evidence.claim: In 1995, lab tests confirmed that CL-77 pigment lots 95-09 and 95-10 exceeded alkalinity specifications, causing AF-12 to gel during accelerated storage.
evidence.quote: Free alkalinity (as PbO): lot 95-07 0.21 %; lot 95-09 0.92 %; lot 95-10 0.88 %. Supplier specification: max 0.30 %.

evidence.title: LABORATORY TEST REPORT LT-1995-118
evidence.claim: In 1995, ammonium chloride was found to neutralize excess alkali in the pigment, preventing livering and maintaining fluid viscosity.
evidence.quote: Ammonium chloride neutralises the excess alkali. Recommendation: add 0.8 kg ammonium chloride per 1000 kg batch as a corrective measure

evidence.title: Laboratory report LT-2020-044 - chloride and drying study, AF-12
evidence.claim: In 2020, ammonium chloride was linked to under-film corrosion complaints on AF-12 coated steel from 2019.
evidence.quote: investigate two complaints of under-film corrosion on AF-12 coated steel (2019). Chloride content of 20 production batches: 380-420 ppm

evidence.title: Laboratory report LT-2020-044 - chloride and drying study, AF-12
evidence.claim: In 2020, tests showed ammonium chloride does not affect drying or viscosity, leading to a recommendation to review its necessity.
evidence.quote: ammonium chloride has no measurable effect on drying. Chloride above 300 ppm can contribute to under-film corrosion on steel.

evidence.title: CHANGE REQUEST CR-1996-005
evidence.claim: In 1996, a chloride limit of 400 ppm was introduced for AF-12 because ammonium chloride can promote under-film corrosion.
evidence.quote: the ammonium chloride addition (CR-1995-009) introduces chloride, which can promote corrosion under the film.

evidence.title: Response to complaint on CL-77 lots 95-09 and 95-10
evidence.claim: In 1995, Cromopigmenti Lazzeretti corrected the CL-77 process to ensure alkalinity was 0.25% or less for all lots from February 1996 onwards.
evidence.quote: The process has been corrected. All lots from 96-02 onwards are released with free alkalinity of 0.25 % or less

evidence.title: Supplier qualification SQ-2007-002 - Fosfazinco Nord S.p.A., ZP-40
evidence.claim: In 2007, trials for a new pigment ZP-40 showed that ammonium chloride was not needed to maintain performance compared to the CL-77 formulation.
evidence.quote: Trial T3 was prepared without the ammonium chloride addition and behaved like T1 and T2.

evidence.title: Compliance memo CM-2006-004: phase-out of lead chromate pigments
evidence.claim: In 2006, the lead chromate pigment CL-77 from Cromopigmenti Lazzeretti was phased out and replaced by zinc phosphate ZP-40.
evidence.quote: basic lead chromate CL-77 will be replaced by zinc phosphate ZP-40 from Fosfazinco Nord

evidence.title: Supplier qualification SQ-2007-002 - Fosfazinco Nord S.p.A., ZP-40
evidence.claim: In 2007, trial batches of AF-12 using ZP-40 pigment showed no livering even when ammonium chloride was omitted.
evidence.quote: Trial T3 was prepared without the ammonium chloride addition

verdict.instruction: Add 1.6 kg ammonium chloride (RM-118) pre-dissolved in 4 L water; stir 10 min.
verdict.reason: The step was added to neutralize high alkalinity in CL-77 pigment to prevent livering (E3, E9). CL-77 was replaced by ZP-40 in 2006 (E15), and 2007 trials confirmed ZP-40 does not require ammonium chloride to prevent livering (E14, E16).
